unreleased: The payment gateway can now ask Stripe's checkout for the payer's billing address and keeps the country Stripe reports with the payment (payment.extra["customer_country"], an upper-case ISO code, already visible to the purpose's on_paid hook) - the basis for VAT place of supply, OSS limits and local taxes. It is opt-in per payment (PaymentQuote.require_billing_address); a purpose that does not set it changes nothing.

Add a tickets module (app/modules/tickets), a ticketing system for administrators only (User.is_admin) that stands on its own and extends the contact form and the CRM when they are enabled: a ticket (numbered from 100001, type Issue / Order / General (the default) / Internal, open or closed) has a thread of internal notes, received messages and e-mails sent to the requester, each entry with the time spent on it (summed in the ticket's header), rich-text content with pictures, and private file attachments (pictures inside the text are served from an unguessable public address so the requester's mail client can show them). Tickets come from three sources: typed in by an administrator (optionally linked to a CRM partner), read every TICKETS_POLL_SECONDS from an IMAP mailbox configured in .env (TICKETS_IMAP_*; a new mail opens a ticket and, with the CRM on, is linked to the partner with the sender's address, otherwise to none), and the contact form - with the module enabled, a message also opens a ticket. Every mail about a ticket carries its number in the subject as "[Ticket#100253] - ..." and Reply-To is the mailbox, so an answer that keeps the number is added to that ticket (and reopens it) instead of opening a new one; mail from our own addresses and automatic mail that names no ticket never opens a ticket, and a mail read twice is filed once. The module manifest can now declare hooks (a module takes part in a flow another module owns, called only while it is enabled; the contact form's "contact_form.received" is the first) and background_tasks (started with the application, cancelled on shutdown; the mailbox poller is the first), and send_email takes reply_to, attachments and headers

Repository module: the LIKE escaping and the reordering of tables, saved filters and statistics each have one shared implementation (reordering an incomplete list of tables now answers the same code, must_list_every_item_once, as the other lists)
Add app/services/sql.py with like_pattern(), the escaping of `%`, `_` and the escape character for a "contains" search, shared by modules instead of copied into each (the CRM module uses it now)

Repository module: an image upload larger than an image may be is refused with 413 before the body is read (by its declared size, or as soon as a body without one has sent too much), instead of being written to disk first; a statistic is computed with one aggregate query (cells, the totals of each dimension and the grand total together) instead of up to four, and the values to be deleted with removed attributes are counted in one query instead of one per attribute
Repository module: an empty slug in an update is refused instead of silently renaming the slug from the name, and only a unique violation on a slug is reported as a taken slug

A record's values may take at most 256 kB all together (a record that is within every attribute's own limits could otherwise add up to tens of megabytes); one that is over the limit is refused with the error `record_too_large`
A saved filter now comes with the records its reference conditions point at (their name, slug and table), so a client can show "Author is Frank Herbert" without a second request

The repository module now saves filters and statistics per table. A filter is a name with the definition of a records query (conditions, sort, deleted records, quick search), checked like a query is, and filters and statistics can be reordered; a statistic is one or two dimensions to group by - text, yes/no, a number, a reference, or a date, date and time or the creation time by day, month or year - and what to compute (count, sum, average, minimum or maximum of a number), optionally over the records of a saved filter, shown as a table, a chart, both or not at all (a pie chart only with one dimension). The server computes the result as a list of groups or, with two dimensions, a pivot table with the totals of every row and column and of everything, computed from the records themselves (so an average total is the average of all the records, not of the averages) and unaffected by cutting the result down to 100 groups or 100 cells; the preview endpoint shows a statistic before it is saved. An attribute that a saved filter or statistic uses cannot be removed from its table, and a filter that a statistic is based on cannot be deleted - the answer lists what uses it. Limits per table: 50 filters and 20 statistics (backend/modules/repository.json)

The repository module now stores records: each has a name and a slug of its own (the slug is made from the name, editable and unique in the table) and a value for any of the table's attributes, checked on the server with a short error code per attribute (text, number, true/false, date, date and time, an image, a reference to a record of the same repository, and lists and maps of one simple type, a list being renumbered whenever its order changes). Records are deleted softly and can be restored, and deleted for good only once deleted and only while no other record refers to them. They are listed a page at a time (25, 50 or 100) with filters by every attribute that has an operator for it (text contains / equals, number comparisons and ranges, dates before / after / between, a chosen record, empty / not empty), a quick search, sorting by any column with empty values last, and a switch for deleted records; a picker endpoint searches a table for a reference. Images (png, jpeg, webp or gif, recognised by their content, never SVG) are uploaded or imported from an address and stored in the database as base64: the server refuses to download from internal addresses (loopback, private, link-local, metadata, redirects included), uploads nobody claims are deleted after a day, and a person's images are limited in size and in total

Add a repository module (app/modules/repository): everyone who is signed in creates their own repositories (databases) with tables whose attributes they define themselves - text, number, boolean, date, date and time, image, a reference to a record of another table of the same repository, and a list or map of one simple type. Everything is private to its owner (somebody else's data answers 404), slugs are made from names and checked live, limits per user live in backend/modules/repository.json, a table's attributes are saved as one ordered list (the type of a saved attribute never changes, and removing one that records hold values for asks for confirmation first), and a repository or table is deleted by confirming its name. Records, images, filters and statistics follow
